title: Set-Associative Mapping: Sets, Ways and the Middle Path
unit: Memory Interfacing, Hierarchy and Cache Mapping
quickIdea: A k-way set-associative cache is direct mapping over sets and full associativity inside a set: set = block mod number of sets, and the k tags in that set are compared in parallel.
remember: Number of sets = lines / k. Index bits = log2(sets) = log2(lines) - log2(k).
Set number = block number mod number of sets, equivalently the index field of the address.
Hardware: k comparators per set, a k-to-1 way-select multiplexer, and a replacement policy that chooses among the k ways.
Direct mapping is k = 1; full associativity is k = lines. Both are special cases of the same address split.
Doubling the associativity at a fixed cache size and block size removes one index bit and adds it to the tag, and halves the number of sets.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2017 Set 1 Q.54: with a direct-mapped cache of N words and block size B words the tag is 10 bits. What is the tag for the same cache built 16-way set-associative?
example.work: Direct: tag = A - log2(N). 16-way: sets = lines/16, so the index loses log2 16 = 4 bits, and those 4 bits move into the tag. Tag = (A - log2 N) + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14.

gateAngle: This is the most repeated question shape in the topic: change the associativity, keep the size, and ask what happens to the tag. The answer never depends on N, B or the address width - only on log2 of the associativity change.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2017 Set 1 Q.54, as worked above.
variations.why: Four index bits become tag bits, so the tag grows by exactly four.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2018 Q.34: with address space 2^P bytes, word length 2^W bytes, cache 2^N bytes, block 2^M words and K-way associativity, what is the tag width?
variations.answer: P - N + log2 K bits (option B).
variations.why: The offset and the index together are N - log2 K bits, so the tag is P minus that. In word units the block offset is M and the set index is N - W - M - log2 K, and they cancel the same way.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A direct-mapped cache of 64 lines with 8-bit tags becomes 4-way set-associative. What is the tag, and how many comparators are there?
variations.answer: 16 sets, so the index falls from 6 to 4 bits and the tag becomes 8 + 2 = 10 bits; four comparators per set, 64 in all.
variations.why: It ties the field change to the hardware cost, which is the other half of the same question.

trap.what: Using the number of lines where the number of sets belongs.
trap.why: The index addresses a set, not a line; using lines overstates the index by log2 k bits and understates the tag by the same amount.
trap.counterexample: GATE CSE 2023 Q.54: a 64 KB 8-way cache with 32-bit addresses has a 19-bit tag whatever the block size is. Using 2^16 lines as the index gives 16 bits of index and a 16-bit tag, which is the popular wrong answer.

check.question: A 2 KB 2-way cache has 64 B blocks and 32-bit addresses. What is the tag width?
check.answer: 32 lines, 16 sets, so index 4; offset 6; tag = 32 - 4 - 6 = 22 bits.
check.explanation: Compare the direct-mapped twin of the same size: 32 lines means index 5 and tag 21, so the 2-way version gained exactly one tag bit.
